title: Den, GTPL: Does a Cable Company Live on Subscriptions?

beats.say: Here is the rule on a channel's price, as notified in twenty seventeen. Take a made up channel at ten rupees a month. The broadcaster must declare at least two rupees as the distributor's share. With discounts, at most three rupees fifty. So does that explain our gap?

beats.say: So, does a cable company live on its subscriptions? Not on those alone. At both companies, booked subscription is the smallest of the three piles. Our reading: a cable connection gives the company the subscriber. It does not set the channels' price. And its fees are agreed with the broadcaster, not set by it alone.
